Full-colour language icons for the docs homepage install tabs and the navbar, provided by the team
(icons.zip, 2026-09-30). Mapping from the zip: Group 25 -> python.svg, Group 23 -> godot.svg,
Group 22 -> flutter.svg, Group 20 -> react-native.svg, Group 19 -> swift.svg, Group 24 -> kotlin.svg.

csharp.svg is a placeholder (plain "C#" text on a purple tile), not from icons.zip and not an official
logo. Replace it with the team's chosen icon.

The logos are trademarks of their owners. Their published guidelines are collected below for reference;
using these icons was a team decision. These notes are not legal advice.

## Sources

Swift (read in full from Apple's PDF)
- https://developer.apple.com/swift/resources/ -> "Download logo and guidelines":
  https://developer.apple.com/swift/downloads/swift-logo.zip -> "Swift Logo Guidelines.pdf" (May 2018)
- p.3: "Developers who are members of the Apple Developer Program can use the Swift logo in promotional
  or technical materials that promote the use of the Swift programming language in their apps."
  "Only the logo versions shown here are approved by Apple. Use logo artwork provided by Apple and do
  not modify the artwork in any way."
- p.4: approved versions are colour, black and white.
- p.5: "The minimum height for the logo is ... 30 pixels for onscreen use."
- p.6: "Do not change the color of the artwork." "Do not use the bird icon alone."
  "Do not use the Swift logo in a running header or footer on every page of your communication."
  "Use only one logo or logo lockup on a communication layout."
  "Do not use the Apple logo on its own or in conjunction with the Swift logo."
- p.9: credit line "The Swift logo is a trademark of Apple Inc."

Kotlin (fetched through a summarising tool; verify wording on the pages)
- https://kotlinlang.org/docs/kotlin-brand-assets.html
  "Do not repaint the logo in third-party colors." "Do not separate the mark from the text."
- https://kotlinfoundation.org/guidelines/ (brand usage guidelines; covers endorsement and use of the icon)

Python (fetched through a summarising tool; verify on the page)
- https://www.python.org/community/logos/
  "please ask first when using a derived version of the logo or when in doubt."

Flutter (fetched through a summarising tool; verify on the page)
- https://flutter.dev/brand
  "Do not alter or use the Flutter mark in a way that may be confusing or misleading."

Godot
- https://godotengine.org/press (fetched through a summarising tool):
  "Godot logos are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International."
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/COPYRIGHT.txt (read verbatim):
  "Files: misc/logo/* / Comment: Godot Engine logo / Copyright: 2017, Andrea Calabró / License: CC-BY-4.0"
  So it needs a credit, e.g. "Godot logo by Andrea Calabró, CC BY 4.0".

React
- No published logo guidelines found. The React logo is a Meta trademark.
